name: Sweet Basil
watering_guidance: Water deeply when the top 1 inch of soil feels dry; avoid wetting foliage directly.
climate_notes: Thrives in warm weather (20°C–30°C / 68°F–86°F). Sensitive to frost and cold snaps.
touch_grass_tip: Pinch flower buds off outdoor stems every Sunday morning to encourage bushy leaf growth.
weekly_tasks: Check topsoil moisture and bottom-water container if dry
Pinch off terminal flower buds to promote bushy leaf production
Inspect underside of leaves for early aphids or spider mites
Harvest top leaves right above a leaf node for kitchen use

name: Cherry Tomato
watering_guidance: Consistent deep watering 2–3 times a week; prevent soil drying out completely to avoid fruit splitting.
climate_notes: Needs at least 6–8 hours of direct sunshine. Check local last frost dates before transplanting outside.
touch_grass_tip: Stake or tie vines to bamboo trellises outside and pinch side suckers in the evening breeze.
weekly_tasks: Secure growing main stem to stake or cage with soft ties
Prune non-fruiting lower suckers to direct energy into fruit clusters
Apply organic liquid potassium fertilizer or compost tea
Check moisture levels to prevent blossom end rot

name: Spearmint
watering_guidance: Loves consistently moist soil. Keep in dedicated container to prevent invasive root spread.
climate_notes: Hardy perennial. Tolerates cool weather and partial shade with ease.
touch_grass_tip: Step outside barefoot, pluck fresh mint sprigs, and crush between fingers for natural aromatherapy.
weekly_tasks: Thoroughly hydrate container and verify drain holes are unblocked
Trim outer runners so roots stay confined to the container
Rotate pot 90 degrees to ensure even sun exposure
Harvest upper third of stems to stimulate fresh young sprigs

name: Baby Spinach
watering_guidance: Keep soil evenly moist. Shallow root system requires frequent light drinks.
climate_notes: Cool-season crop; bolts (goes to seed) when summer temperatures exceed 25°C (77°F).
touch_grass_tip: Sow succession seeds outdoors every two weeks for a continuous fresh salad harvest.
weekly_tasks: Weed around shallow roots gently with fingers
Thin out crowded seedlings to 3 inches apart
Mulch lightly with shredded straw to keep soil cool and damp
Harvest outer leaves, leaving center crown to keep growing

name: Tuscan Rosemary
watering_guidance: Allow top 2 inches of soil to completely dry out before watering. Highly drought-tolerant.
climate_notes: Mediterranean native. Needs well-draining sandy/loamy soil and full sun; hates soggy roots.
touch_grass_tip: Run your fingers along the outdoor woody branches every morning for an energizing pine scent.
seasonal_timing: Year-round in temperate zones; Spring planting elsewhere
weekly_tasks: Test soil dryness with finger before adding any water
Check pot drainage hole to ensure zero stagnant standing water
Trim 2-inch tip cuttings for kitchen seasoning and branching
Ensure container receives maximum direct south-facing sunlight

name: Sweet Bell Pepper
watering_guidance: Deep watering every 3–4 days; mulch surface to maintain steady root zone moisture.
climate_notes: Requires warm soil (>18°C/65°F) to set fruit. Shield from heavy gales.
touch_grass_tip: Gently shake flowering branches around midday outside to boost self-pollination.
weekly_tasks: Gently stake central pepper branch to support heavy fruits
Apply organic tomato-and-pepper feed rich in phosphorus
Scout for hornworms or leafhoppers on underside of foliage
Lightly mist blossoms early morning if humidity is exceptionally low

name: Butterhead Lettuce
watering_guidance: Water at the soil level every 1–2 days. Sensitive to drought.
climate_notes: Superb for cool seasons and partial sunlight. Protect from blazing afternoon sun.
touch_grass_tip: Sit in the patio breeze at dusk and pluck tender outer leaves for tonight's salad.
weekly_tasks: Inspect planter for slugs or snails under leaf folds
Refresh mulch barrier to prevent soil splashing onto tender leaves
Provide light afternoon shade cloth if temperatures spike
Harvest lowest mature leaves using the 'cut-and-come-again' method

name: English Lavender
watering_guidance: Very sparse watering. Let soil dry out almost entirely; gritty, aerated soil required.
climate_notes: Needs strong sun and excellent air circulation. Dislikes tropical humidity and overwatering.
touch_grass_tip: Bask in the outdoor garden bed while listening to honeybees drawn to purple lavender spikes.
weekly_tasks: Check soil aerator holes to confirm no damp stagnation
Deadhead spent flower stalks right down to the leaf mound
Prune lightly to maintain rounded habit without cutting old wood
Collect harvested flower stems into dried outdoor sachets

name: French Breakfast Radish
watering_guidance: Consistent even moisture; dry spells cause woody, overly pungent roots.
climate_notes: Fastest growing edible crop! Perfect for fast wins in temperate, cool seasons.
touch_grass_tip: Get your hands into the garden bed soil and feel the crisp radish bulbs swelling under the surface.
weekly_tasks: Thin seedlings to 2 inches apart to allow bulb expansion
Gently earth up exposed shoulders to prevent greening
Keep soil weed-free so shallow root development is unrestricted
Pull up mature 1-inch crisp bulbs and wash with hose outdoors

name: French Marigold
watering_guidance: Water moderately when soil surface feels dry. Very forgiving.
climate_notes: Attracts pollinators while repelling garden pests like nematodes and aphids naturally.
touch_grass_tip: Deadhead spent blooms outside with your fingers to stimulate non-stop golden flowers.
weekly_tasks: Pinch off faded flowers with fingers to spur new bud clusters
Inspect companion plants nearby for decreased pest activity
Give moderate watering directly around base
Collect dry mature seed heads in an envelope for next season

name: Ever-bearing Strawberries
watering_guidance: Provide 1 inch of water weekly; keep crown above soil level to avoid rot.
climate_notes: Perennial that thrives in hanging baskets, raised beds, or patio planters with sun.
touch_grass_tip: Hang a basket on the patio or balcony railing and graze on sun-warmed berries straight from the vine.
weekly_tasks: Tuck clean straw or gravel underneath hanging berries to avoid soil contact
Clip excess runners so the mother plant pours strength into fruit
Monitor for curious birds and drape light mesh if needed
Check crowns to ensure soil hasn't washed over growing points

name: Sansevieria (Snake Plant)
watering_guidance: Extremely drought-hardy. Water only once every 2–3 weeks; allow soil to dry completely.
climate_notes: Indestructible architectural plant. Handles low-light corners and shaded balconies.
touch_grass_tip: Wipe sword-like leaves with a damp cloth outdoors to maximize oxygen release and dust capture.
weekly_tasks: Assess soil with a wooden skewer to ensure bone-dry before watering
Wipe broad architectural leaves with damp cloth to clean dust
Rotate container toward gentle ambient light for upright habit
Inspect base for new upright shoots ('pups') sprouting in pot

name: Golden Pothos
watering_guidance: Water when top 50% of potting mix dries out. Forgiving if neglected.
climate_notes: Tolerates low light and high humidity. Perfect for sheltered balconies and dim apartment rooms.
touch_grass_tip: Train trailing green vines along balcony trellises or bookshelves for a cascading jungle vibe.
weekly_tasks: Check leaf firmness; water only if top half of pot is dry
Trim trailing vines and place cuttings in water to root new plants
Mist leaves or clean foliage in the gentle morning air
Guide trailing tendrils along support wires or hooks

name: English Thyme
watering_guidance: Water deeply only when soil is completely dry. Needs sharp drainage.
climate_notes: Hardy perennial. Creates fragrant carpeting in garden beds or compact balcony pots.
touch_grass_tip: Brush your boot or hand across thyme leaves to release uplifting herbal essential oils outside.
weekly_tasks: Check that drainage hole flows freely without pooling
Prune woody stems by one-third to encourage tender young sprigs
Sun-dry freshly snipped stems on a garden tray
Mulch base with coarse gravel to reflect warmth to lower stems

name: Lacinato Tuscan Kale
watering_guidance: 1 to 1.5 inches of water per week. Consistent moisture keeps leaves sweet.
climate_notes: Flavor sweetens remarkably after light autumn frosts. High cold resilience.
touch_grass_tip: Visit the garden on brisk mornings to pick crisp dinosaur kale leaves directly for cooking.
weekly_tasks: Inspect underside of crinkled leaves for cabbage looper eggs
Top-dress soil with well-rotted garden compost or worm castings
Harvest bottom palm-like leaves while preserving center stalk
Check root zone dampness with garden trowel

name: Black Beauty Zucchini
watering_guidance: Heavy drinker; water deeply at soil line 2–3 times a week, avoiding leaves.
climate_notes: Rapid vigorous grower needing warm soil and space to sprawl (minimum 3 ft diameter).
touch_grass_tip: Check the morning blossoms outside and spot bees buzzing between male and female yellow flowers.
weekly_tasks: Check under wide leaves daily for rapidly expanding squash
Remove older yellowing bottom leaves with clean shears for airflow
Water soil directly in early morning to prevent powdery mildew
Harvest zucchinis at 6–8 inches for peak tender flavor

name: Boston Fern
watering_guidance: Keep soil moist but not soggy. Thrives with misting and high humidity.
climate_notes: Excellent for shady covered balconies or damp rooms out of harsh direct sun rays.
touch_grass_tip: Hang in a shaded outdoor porch corner and mist fronds on humid summer afternoons.
weekly_tasks: Check soil moisture beneath lush fronds
Mist fronds gently with lukewarm water
Trim brown or dried outer leaflets at base
Turn hanging basket to ensure balanced frond draping
